title: Stagecraft: All-team slate + townline rehearsal notes (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose
----
This doc is a working rehearsal and message slate for the Q3 all-team townline (internal-facing). It combines a compact OKR draft, top-level exec updates, the run-of-show for the live session, and an 'open-mic' plan for IC participation. Use as the single source for rehearsal, AV check, and pre-brief followups.

High-level goals for the all-team
- Create a clear, shared view of what matters next 90 days: three prioritized company threads (Performance & Cost, Private Deployments, Developer-ecosystem momentum).
- Surface measurable asks to teams (who owns which cross-team deliveries).
- Land messages that reduce emergent questions post-townline and create clear follow-up signals (tickets, office hours, team drop-ins).

Draft company OKRs (compact, will be refined by leadership review)
Objective A: Make serving predictable and cheaper for production applications
- KR A1: Reduce 95th percentile token-latency for hosted API by 15% vs baseline (Q2 end).
- KR A2: Lower per-token cost for top 10 customer workloads by 20% through batching/caching recommendations and quantization profiles.
- KR A3: Ship support for two new quantized model variants in Redwood Optimize catalog with verified perf/regression tests.

Objective B: Expand enterprise adoption of Dedicated and Private modes
- KR B1: Close 6 new Dedicated contracts (monthly reserved capacity) with CFO-level SLAs.
- KR B2: Onboard 3 regulated customers to Private VPC or on-prem package with completed SOC2 readiness checklist.
- KR B3: Reduce onboarding time from saleshandshake to first serving request to <30 days for Dedicated.

Objective C: Improve developer experience to accelerate product usage and retention
- KR C1: Increase API self-serve activation rate by 25% (measured as first meaningful inference within 7 days).
- KR C2: Launch two SDK improvements (streaming & function-calling examples) and 10 new quickstart templates.
- KR C3: Maintain model-quality SLA: <1.5% regression incidents in production per quarter tied to model rollouts.

Notes on OKRs
- These are intentionally compact — we will surface team-level KRs after the exec sync. Expect product/serving/runtime owners to break these down.
- Open question: Do we present per-customer case studies (privacy OK) or anonymized impact numbers? (Action: comms + legal to confirm by 2026-07-18).

Exec update bullet points (talking points for founders/execs)
- Lead message (30s): We are prioritizing performance economics — better latency at lower unit cost, and making Dedicated/Private choices easier to buy and faster to adopt.
- Metrics to surface: 95p latency, cost-per-1K tokens (hosted vs dedicated), Dedicated pipeline funnel (MQL->POC->Closed), activation conversion.
- Risk callouts to be briefed: cloud region outages contingency, supply-chain variance for Dedicated GPU capacity, and one outstanding SOC2 control.

Run-of-show (45–60 minute townline)
- 0:00–0:03 Welcome + framing (CEO) — tight opener, share three threads and desired team outcomes.
- 0:03–0:10 Product/Serving highlights (SVP Product + Eng lead) — 2 slides, 1 demo snippet (streaming + fallback demo).
- 0:10–0:20 OKR snapshot & asks (Head of Strategy) — call out KR owners and alignment ladder.
- 0:20–0:30 Customer & Sales spot (GTM) — 1 customer highlight + Dedicated pipeline asks.
- 0:30–0:40 Team spotlight (two 4-minute lightning updates): Optimize toolkit & Private onboarding playbook.
- 0:40–0:55 Open-mic (moderated) — pre-submitted Qs prioritized, live mic for up to 4 ICs (max 2 min each).
- 0:55–1:00 Close + next steps (Ops) — office hours slots, follow-up doc link, action owners.

Open-mic plan and moderation
- Encourage pre-submissions via the Google Form (linked artifact). We will use pre-submissions to seed the live queue.
- Moderator (Elena Park) will triage to ensure high-signal questions; reserve two slots for live volunteer questions.
- Timeboxing: max 2 minutes speaker + 1 min follow-up. If lots of volume, move deep dives to breakout office hours.

Rehearsal checklist (what to validate in the run-through)
- Slide timing: each segment owner runs a 5-minute dry run with comms.
- Demo readiness: staged dataset, network emulation for streaming demo to surface a fallback.
- AV: mics checked, remote presenter pass, stage view set (slide master + company video intro). (Action: Facilities/IT to confirm by 2026-07-13).
- Recording: set to internal-only, captions on, transcript capture.
- Backchannel: #all-hands-rehearsal Slack channel open for live cueing.

Roles and ownership (pre-show and during show)
- Host/MC: CEO (framing) + Ops co-host (timekeeping)
- Moderator: Elena Park (open-mic triage)
- Tech run lead: Samir Gupta (demo + AV)
- Comms lead: Lena Rodriguez (slides + consistent messaging + postcard)
- Follow-up coordinator: Arjun Patel (action tracker + office hours scheduling)

Key messages & scripts (short templates)
- For founders: "We are doubling down on predictable serving economics — expect visible latency and unit-cost wins this quarter; ops will get playbooks to adopt new profiles."
- For Eng teams: "Your priority is shipping tested quantization variants and validating batch/caching suggestions on canaries — product will schedule rollout windows with each team."
- For GTM/Sales: "Focus deals where Dedicated gives clear ROI — we will provide pocket decks and TCO comparisons for customer conversations."

Follow-up and signal plan
- Publish post-townline note with: recording, 1-page OKR summary, action tracker with owners + deadlines, and sign-up for office hours. (Responsible: Arjun Patel — publish by 2026-07-17).
- Triage high-volume questions into Jira (label: allhands-q3-2026) and track resolution in the action tracker.

Risks & contingency playbook (short)
- If demo fails: pivot to prerecorded capture + live Q&A.
- If large-volume open-mic derails timings: close live mic and open distributed office hours same day.
- If an exec has to drop: pre-record their 60–90s message and have MC play it with a brief live follow-on.

Unresolved items / decisions needed
- Legal sign-off on whether we can include anonymized customer impact snapshots (due 2026-07-18).
- Final OKR alignment meeting with Eng leads (schedule: 2026-07-12).
- Confirm Dedicated contract closes to highlight as customer story by 2026-07-20.

Quick to-dos (next 72 hours)
- Lena: finalize executive slides and 1-page OKR summary (due 2026-07-12).
- Samir: full AV run and demo smoke test (due 2026-07-13).
- Elena: open-mic form live and Comm pre-scrub (due 2026-07-11).
- Arjun: create action-tracker template in Google Sheet and link to doc (due 2026-07-11).

Appendix: rehearsal notes (raw)
- 2026-07-10, 10:30am — dry run with product: streaming demo stutters at 12k token window; mitigate with shorter context in live demo.
- 2026-07-11, 09:00am — comms suggested reducing exec slides to 3 bullets each to keep pace.
- Slack thread with rehearsal comments: see Slack:#all-hands-rehearsal (linked artifact).

Questions for reviewers
- Is the OKR compactness acceptable for exec buy-in or do we need more granular KRs for the townline?
- How comfortable are we with the open-mic format for a 150-person internal audience (safety / moderation rules)?

If you're assigned an action above, please drop confirmation in #all-hands-rehearsal and update the action tracker when complete. This doc will be iterated after each rehearsal until final.
